days.day: Thursday of week 33 in Ordinary Time
days.name: Thursday of week 33 in Ordinary Time
days.week: Thursday of week 33 in Ordinary Time

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: And when he drew near, seeing the city, he wept over it, saying:
If thou also hadst known, and that in this thy day, the things that are to thy peace; but now they are hidden from thy eyes.
For the days shall come upon thee, and thy enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and compass thee round, and straiten thee on every side,
And beat thee flat to the ground, and thy children who are in thee: and they shall not leave in thee a stone upon a stone: because thou hast not known the time of thy visitation.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: If thou also hadst known, and that in this thy day, the things that are to thy peace; but now they are hidden from thy eyes.

days.title: HE CRIED OVER THE CITY
days.t: Jesus looks at the city he loves and cries. Peace was right in front of it and it missed it.
days.where: Jesus is coming down the Mount of Olives toward Jerusalem, a few days before he dies. The crowd is celebrating, and he stops and weeps, because he can see the city is going to turn him away. About forty years later the Romans did tear Jerusalem down.
days.means: God doesn't watch us blow it with his arms crossed. He cries over it. The visit is today, not someday, and the things that bring peace are usually sitting right there if we stop long enough to see them.
days.today: Name one thing that actually brings you peace, and make time for it today instead of later.
days.say: Jesus, don't let me miss you when you show up. Open my eyes to what brings me peace today. Amen.

days.day: Friday of week 33 in Ordinary Time
days.name: Friday of week 33 in Ordinary Time
days.week: Friday of week 33 in Ordinary Time

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: And entering into the temple, he began to cast out them that sold therein, and them that bought.
Saying to them: It is written: My house is the house of prayer. But you have made it a den of thieves.
And he was teaching daily in the temple. And the chief priests and the scribes and the rulers of the people sought to destroy him:
And they found not what to do to him: for all the people were very attentive to hear him.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: My house is the house of prayer. But you have made it a den of thieves.

days.title: HE FLIPPED THE TABLES
days.t: Jesus walks into the Temple and throws the sellers out. God's house is for prayer, not a hustle.
days.where: This is right after Jesus rides into Jerusalem, days before he dies. The Temple courtyard had turned into a market, with sellers and money changers working the crowds who came to pray.
days.means: Jesus gets angry about what people do to the place where God meets them. You are a temple too. Whatever has set up shop in there and crowded out prayer, he wants to clear it out.
days.today: Clear one thing out of your day that crowds out God, even for ten minutes.
days.say: Jesus, walk into my heart and clear out what doesn't belong there. Make me a house of prayer. Amen.

days.day: The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary on Saturday of week 33 in Ordinary Time
days.name: The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
days.week: Saturday of week 33 in Ordinary Time

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: And there came to him some of the Sadducees, who deny that there is any resurrection, and they asked him,
Saying: Master, Moses wrote unto us, If any man’s brother die, having a wife, and he leave no children, that his brother should take her to wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.
There were therefore seven brethren: and the first took a wife, and died without children.
And the next took her to wife, and he also died childless.
And the third took her. And in like manner all the seven, and they left no children, and died.
Last of all the woman died also.
In the resurrection therefore, whose wife of them shall she be? For all the seven had her to wife.
And Jesus said to them: The children of this world marry, and are given in marriage:
But they that shall be accounted worthy of that world, and of the resurrection from the dead, shall neither be married, nor take wives.
Neither can they die any more: for they are equal to the angels, and are the children of God, being the children of the resurrection.
Now that the dead rise again, Moses also shewed, at the bush, when he called the Lord, The God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob;
For he is not the God of the dead, but of the living: for all live to him.
And some of the scribes answering, said to him: Master, thou hast said well.
And after that they durst not ask him any more questions.

saint.name: The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
saint.about: An old tradition, not from the Bible but from an early Christian writing, says Mary's parents, Joachim and Anne, brought her to the Temple in Jerusalem as a little girl to give her to God. The Church keeps this day to honor how Mary belonged to God from the very start.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: For he is not the God of the dead, but of the living: for all live to him.

days.title: GOD OF THE LIVING
days.t: Some people tried to trap Jesus with a trick question about heaven. He told them the dead are alive to God.
days.where: The Sadducees, a group of priests who didn't believe in the resurrection, make up a story about a woman married seven times to make the whole idea sound silly. Jesus answers them straight from Moses.
days.means: Heaven isn't just this life on repeat. It's something bigger than we can picture. And the people we've lost aren't gone to God. Everybody you pray for is alive to him.
days.today: Say a prayer for someone you've lost, by name.
days.say: God of the living, hold the people I miss close to you. Let me see them again someday. Amen.

days.name: Our Lord Jesus Christ, King of the Universe

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: And when the Son of man shall come in his majesty, and all the angels with him, then shall he sit upon the seat of his majesty.
And all nations shall be gathered together before him, and he shall separate them one from another, as the shepherd separateth the sheep from the goats:
And he shall set the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on his left.
Then shall the king say to them that shall be on his right hand: Come, ye blessed of my Father, possess you the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.
For I was hungry, and you gave me to eat; I was thirsty, and you gave me to drink; I was a stranger, and you took me in:
Naked, and you covered me: sick, and you visited me: I was in prison, and you came to me.
Then shall the just answer him, saying: Lord, when did we see thee hungry, and fed thee; thirsty, and gave thee drink?
And when did we see thee a stranger, and took thee in? or naked, and covered thee?
Or when did we see thee sick or in prison, and came to thee?
And the king answering, shall say to them: Amen I say to you, as long as you did it to one of these my least brethren, you did it to me.
Then he shall say to them also that shall be on his left hand: Depart from me, you cursed, into everlasting fire which was prepared for the devil and his angels.
For I was hungry, and you gave me not to eat: I was thirsty, and you gave me not to drink.
I was a stranger, and you took me not in: naked, and you covered me not: sick and in prison, and you did not visit me.
Then they also shall answer him, saying: Lord, when did we see thee hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and did not minister to thee?
Then he shall answer them, saying: Amen I say to you, as long as you did it not to one of these least, neither did you do it to me.
And these shall go into everlasting punishment: but the just, into life everlasting.

saint.name: Christ the King
saint.about: Pope Pius XI started this feast in 1925, when dictators and big governments were trying to take the place of God. It says no leader, party or paycheck gets the last word: Jesus does. It's the last Sunday of the Church year.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: Amen I say to you, as long as you did it to one of these my least brethren, you did it to me.

days.title: THE KING IN DISGUISE
days.t: The King of everything shows up as the hungry guy, the stranger, the one in jail. How you treat them is how you treat him.
days.where: Jesus tells this right before his Passion: at the end, the Son of Man sits as king and sorts people like a shepherd sorts sheep from goats. The surprise is that nobody on either side knew it was him.
days.means: Today closes out the Church's year, and next Sunday Advent starts. Christ is King, but his throne room is the street. Feeding someone, visiting someone, showing up for someone is serving the King himself.
days.today: Do one thing for somebody who can't pay you back: food, a ride, a visit, a call.
days.say: Jesus, my King, help me see you in the people everybody else walks past. Rule my heart. Amen.

days.day: Monday of week 34 in Ordinary Time or Saint Clement I, Pope, Martyr or Saint Columbanus, Abbot and Missionary or Blessed Miguel Agustín Pro, Martyr
days.name: Monday of week 34 in Ordinary Time
days.week: Monday of week 34 in Ordinary Time

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: And looking on, he saw the rich men cast their gifts into the treasury.
And he saw also a certain poor widow casting in two brass mites.
And he said: Verily I say to you, that this poor widow hath cast in more than they all:
For all these have of their abundance cast into the offerings of God: but she of her want, hath cast in all the living that she had.

saint.name: Blessed Miguel Agustín Pro
saint.about: A Mexican Jesuit priest who said Mass and gave the sacraments in secret, in disguises, when the government of Mexico was persecuting the Church. He was executed by firing squad in Mexico City, his arms stretched out like a cross, saying 'Viva Cristo Rey,' long live Christ the King.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: Verily I say to you, that this poor widow hath cast in more than they all

days.title: TWO LITTLE COINS
days.t: Rich people drop big gifts in the Temple box. A poor widow drops two tiny coins, and Jesus says she gave the most.
days.where: Jesus is in the Temple in Jerusalem during his last days, watching people bring their offerings. The widow's two coins were the smallest money there was, and it was everything she had to live on.
days.means: God doesn't count it like we do. He looks at the heart behind the gift. Small and all-in beats big and leftover, whether it's money, time or love.
days.today: Give somebody your full attention today, phone down, even if it's only five minutes.
days.say: Lord, I don't have much, but what I have is yours. Take it all. Amen.

days.day: Saints Andrew Dũng-Lạc and his Companions, Martyrs on Tuesday of week 34 in Ordinary Time
days.name: Saints Andrew Dũng-Lạc and Companions
days.week: Tuesday of week 34 in Ordinary Time

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: And some saying of the temple, that it was adorned with goodly stones and gifts, he said:
These things which you see, the days will come in which there shall not be left a stone upon a stone that shall not be thrown down.
And they asked him, saying: Master, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign when they shall begin to come to pass?
Who said: Take heed you be not seduced; for many will come in my name, saying, I am he; and the time is at hand: go ye not therefore after them.
And when you shall hear of wars and seditions, be not terrified: these things must first come to pass; but the end is not yet presently.
Then he said to them: Nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
And there shall be great earthquakes in divers places, and pestilences, and famines, and terrors from heaven; and there shall be great signs.

saint.name: Saints Andrew Dũng-Lạc and Companions
saint.about: 117 martyrs of Vietnam: priests, catechists, mothers, fathers and soldiers killed for the faith over more than a hundred years. Andrew Dũng-Lạc was a Vietnamese priest who was beheaded in 1839. Saint John Paul II made them saints in 1988.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: And when you shall hear of wars and seditions, be not terrified

days.title: DON'T PANIC
days.t: Jesus says scary days will come, wars and earthquakes and all of it. And he says don't be terrified.
days.where: People are admiring how beautiful the Temple is, and Jesus tells them it will be torn down. He's talking near the end of his life about hard times coming for the world and for his followers.
days.means: Bad news doesn't mean God lost control. Jesus told us ahead of time so we wouldn't freak out or follow whoever yells the loudest. Fear doesn't get to drive.
days.today: Take a break from the news or the feed today and pray for one place that's hurting.
days.say: Jesus, when the world feels like it's falling apart, keep me calm and close to you. Amen.

days.day: Wednesday of week 34 in Ordinary Time or Saint Catherine of Alexandria, Virgin, Martyr
days.name: Wednesday of week 34 in Ordinary Time
days.week: Wednesday of week 34 in Ordinary Time

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: But before all these things, they will lay their hands upon you, and persecute you, delivering you up to the synagogues and into prisons, dragging you before kings and governors, for my name’s sake.
And it shall happen unto you for a testimony.
Lay it up therefore into your hearts, not to meditate before how you shall answer:
For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to resist and gainsay.
And you shall be betrayed by your parents and brethren, and kinsmen and friends; and some of you they will put to death.
And you shall be hated by all men for my name’s sake.
But a hair of your head shall not perish.
In your patience you shall possess your souls.

saint.name: Saint Catherine of Alexandria
saint.about: A young woman of Alexandria in Egypt, remembered as a sharp mind who stood up for the faith in front of the emperor's scholars and was martyred for it. She is a patron of students and philosophers.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: In your patience you shall possess your souls.

days.title: HOLD ON
days.t: Jesus warns his friends they'll get dragged, doubted and even turned on by their own people. Then he says hang in there, and you keep your soul.
days.where: Jesus is in Jerusalem in his last days, telling his followers what's coming for them after he's gone. Not one hair of your head will be lost, he says.
days.means: Following Jesus was never sold as easy. But the people who stay steady, who don't quit when it gets ugly, are the ones who come out whole. Patience is how you keep yourself.
days.today: When something tests you today, wait ten seconds before you answer. Let it pass through you.
days.say: Jesus, give me the patience to stay steady when people come at me. Keep my soul in your hands. Amen.

days.day: Thanksgiving Day on Thursday of week 34 in Ordinary Time
days.name: Thanksgiving Day
days.week: Thursday of week 34 in Ordinary Time

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: And it came to pass, as he was going to Jerusalem, he passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.
And as he entered into a certain town, there met him ten men that were lepers, who stood afar off;
And lifted up their voice, saying: Jesus, master, have mercy on us.
Whom when he saw, he said: Go, shew yourselves to the priests. And it came to pass, as they went, they were made clean.
And one of them, when he saw that he was made clean, went back, with a loud voice glorifying God.
And he fell on his face before his feet, giving thanks: and this was a Samaritan.
And Jesus answering, said, Were not ten made clean? and where are the nine?
There is no one found to return and give glory to God, but this stranger.
And he said to him: Arise, go thy way; for thy faith hath made thee whole.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: Were not ten made clean? and where are the nine?

days.title: WHERE ARE THE NINE
days.t: Jesus heals ten sick men at once. Only one comes back to say thank you.
days.where: Jesus is walking toward Jerusalem along the border of Samaria and Galilee. Ten men with leprosy, cut off from everybody, call out to him. On the way to the priests they're healed, and only the outsider, a Samaritan, turns around.
days.means: All ten got the miracle. One got the friendship. Saying thank you is what turns a blessing into a relationship with the one who gave it. The word Eucharist itself means thanksgiving.
days.today: Before you eat today, say out loud one thing you're thankful for. Then text one person thank you.
days.say: Lord, you've done more for me than I can count. Let me be the one who comes back to say thank you. Amen.

days.day: Friday of week 34 in Ordinary Time
days.name: Friday of week 34 in Ordinary Time
days.week: Friday of week 34 in Ordinary Time

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: And he spoke to them in a similitude. See the fig tree, and all the trees:
When they now shoot forth their fruit, you know that summer is nigh;
So you also, when you shall see these things come to pass, know that the kingdom of God is at hand.
Amen, I say to you, this generation shall not pass away, till all things be fulfilled.
Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.

days.title: HIS WORDS DON'T FADE
days.t: Jesus says you can tell summer's close when the fig tree starts to bud, and you can read God's signs the same way. Then he says heaven and earth will pass away, but his words never will.
days.where: Jesus is in the Temple in Jerusalem in his last days, talking about the end of the world. It's the last week of the Church's year, so the readings are all about the end, and about what lasts.
days.means: Trends fade, phones die, and even this world won't last forever. What Jesus says stays true through all of it. Build your life on his words and you're standing on the one thing that won't fall.
days.today: Pick one thing Jesus said and keep it where you'll see it all day, on your lock screen or a sticky note.
days.say: Jesus, everything around me keeps changing. You don't. Let your words be the ground I stand on. Amen.

days.day: Saturday of week 34 in Ordinary Time or Saturday memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary
days.name: Saturday of week 34 in Ordinary Time
days.week: Saturday of week 34 in Ordinary Time

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: And take heed to yourselves, lest perhaps your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting and drunkenness, and the cares of this life, and that day come upon you suddenly.
For as a snare shall it come upon all that sit upon the face of the whole earth.
Watch ye, therefore, praying at all times, that you may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that are to come, and to stand before the Son of man.

saint.name: Saturday memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary
saint.about: On Saturdays with no other feast, the Church can give the day to Mary, a custom more than a thousand years old. Advent is about to begin, the season of waiting for Jesus, and nobody waited for him like his mother did.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: Take heed to yourselves, lest perhaps your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting and drunkenness, and the cares of this life

days.title: KEEP YOUR HEART LIGHT
days.t: Jesus says don't let your heart get weighed down, by partying too hard or by the stress of life, or his day will catch you off guard. Stay awake and keep praying.
days.where: These are the last words of Jesus' long talk in the Temple about the end. It's the last day of the Church's year: Advent starts with tonight's vigil Masses, and the wait for Christmas begins.
days.means: This isn't Jesus against a good time. He went to weddings too. He's talking about a heart so heavy it stops looking up. Keep yours light enough to notice when God shows up.
days.today: Before you go out tonight, or before you fall asleep, say one short prayer. Even just: Lord, I'm here.
days.say: Lord, take the weight off my heart. Keep me awake and ready for you. Amen.

days.name: First Sunday of Advent

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: Take ye heed, watch and pray. For ye know not when the time is.
Even as a man who going into a far country, left his house; and gave authority to his servants over every work, and commanded the porter to watch.
Watch ye therefore, (for you know not when the lord of the house cometh: at even, or at midnight, or at the cockcrowing, or in the morning,)
Lest coming on a sudden, he find you sleeping.
And what I say to you, I say to all: Watch.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: Watch ye therefore... Lest coming on a sudden, he find you sleeping.

days.title: DON'T SLEEP ON IT
days.t: Jesus says stay awake, because nobody knows when he's coming back: evening, midnight, when the rooster crows or at sunrise. Don't let him find you asleep.
days.where: Jesus is sitting on the Mount of Olives across from the Temple, telling Peter, James, John and Andrew about the end of time. He ends with a story about a man who leaves home and tells the doorkeeper to stay up and watch for him.
days.means: Today Advent starts, and a new Church year with it. The color turns violet, and we get four Sundays to get ready: for Christmas, when Jesus came the first time, and for the day he comes back. Advent isn't about being scared. It's about being awake when he walks in.
days.today: Light a candle tonight, the first one on the Advent wreath if your family has one, and tell God what you're waiting on.
days.say: Come, Lord Jesus. Wake me up. Keep my heart ready for you, this Christmas and the day you come back. Amen.

days.name: Saint Andrew

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: And Jesus walking by the sea of Galilee, saw two brethren, Simon who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea (for they were fishers).
And he saith to them: Come ye after me, and I will make you to be fishers of men.
And they immediately leaving their nets, followed him.
And going on from thence, he saw other two brethren, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets: and he called them.
And they forthwith left their nets and father, and followed him.

saint.name: Saint Andrew
saint.about: A fisherman from Bethsaida and Simon Peter's brother, and a follower of John the Baptist before he followed Jesus. The Eastern Churches call him the First-Called. Tradition says he died on an X-shaped cross in Greece. He's a patron of Scotland and of fishermen, and many families start the Saint Andrew Christmas prayer today and say it every day until Christmas.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: Come ye after me, and I will make you to be fishers of men. And they immediately leaving their nets, followed him.

days.title: DROP THE NETS
days.t: Jesus walks up to two brothers fishing, Simon Peter and Andrew, and says come follow me. They drop their nets right there and go.
days.where: It's the Sea of Galilee, near the start of Jesus' public life. Andrew and Peter fished for a living. A little farther down the shore Jesus calls two more brothers, James and John, and they leave their boat and their father to follow him.
days.means: Andrew didn't wait until he had it all figured out. Jesus called and he moved. In John's Gospel, the first thing Andrew does after meeting Jesus is go get his brother. Saying yes to Jesus is never just for you.
days.today: Do what Andrew did: invite one person, your brother, a cousin, a friend, to come to Mass with you Sunday.
days.say: Saint Andrew, pray for us. Jesus, when you call, help me drop what I'm holding and follow you. Amen.

days.day: Tuesday of the 1st week of Advent
days.name: Tuesday of the 1st week of Advent
days.week: Tuesday of the 1st week of Advent

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: In that same hour, he rejoiced in the Holy Ghost, and said: I confess to thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because thou hast hidden these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them to little ones. Yea, Father, for so it hath seemed good in thy sight.
All things are delivered to me by my Father; and no one knoweth who the Son is, but the Father; and who the Father is, but the Son, and to whom the Son will reveal him.
And turning to his disciples, he said: Blessed are the eyes that see the things which you see.
For I say to you, that many prophets and kings have desired to see the things that you see, and have not seen them; and to hear the things that you hear, and have not heard them.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: thou hast hidden these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them to little ones.

days.title: NO DEGREE NEEDED
days.t: Jesus is filled with joy and thanks the Father for showing the truth to little ones, not to the people who think they know it all. Then he tells his friends they're blessed to see what they're seeing.
days.where: Jesus just sent out seventy two disciples two by two, and they came back hyped about what God did through them. This is his answer. The first reading is Isaiah's promise of a shoot growing out of the stump of Jesse, a king who will finally bring peace.
days.means: You don't have to be the smartest person in the room to know God. He shows himself to people who come to him like kids: honest, open, ready to be amazed. Being humble isn't being dumb. It's leaving room for God to teach you something.
days.today: Ask God one honest question today, the kind you'd be embarrassed to ask out loud, and stay quiet a minute after.
days.say: Father, I don't have it all figured out. Make me little enough to hear you, and let me see what you're showing me. Amen.

days.day: Wednesday of the 1st week of Advent
days.name: Wednesday of the 1st week of Advent
days.week: Wednesday of the 1st week of Advent

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: And when Jesus had passed away from thence, he came nigh the sea of Galilee. And going up into a mountain, he sat there.
And there came to him great multitudes, having with them the dumb, the blind, the lame, the maimed, and many others: and they cast them down at his feet, and he healed them:
So that the multitudes marvelled seeing the dumb speak, the lame walk, and the blind see: and they glorified the God of Israel.

And Jesus called together his disciples, and said: I have compassion on the multitudes, because they continue with me now three days, and have not what to eat, and I will not send them away fasting, lest they faint in the way.
And the disciples say unto him: Whence then should we have so many loaves in the desert, as to fill so great a multitude?
And Jesus said to them: How many loaves have you? But they said: Seven, and a few little fishes.
And he commanded the multitude to sit down upon the ground.
And taking the seven loaves and the fishes, and giving thanks, he brake, and gave to his disciples, and the disciples to the people.
And they did all eat, and had their fill. And they took up seven baskets full, of what remained of the fragments.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: I have compassion on the multitudes... and I will not send them away fasting, lest they faint in the way.

days.title: NOBODY LEAVES HUNGRY
days.t: Crowds bring Jesus everyone who's hurting and he heals them. After three days with him the people have nothing left to eat, so he takes seven loaves and a few fish, gives thanks, and feeds them all, with seven baskets left over.
days.where: Jesus is on a mountain by the Sea of Galilee. The first reading is Isaiah's picture of God throwing a feast for every nation on his mountain and wiping the tears off every face. The Psalm today is the Lord is my shepherd.
days.means: Jesus notices when you're running on empty. He doesn't send people home with nothing. Look at what he does with the bread: he takes it, gives thanks, breaks it and gives it. That's what the priest does at every Mass, and in the Eucharist he still feeds us with himself.
days.today: Bring someone something to eat today, a snack for a coworker, a plate for your grandma, and don't make it a big deal.
days.say: Jesus, you see when I'm tired and empty. Feed me, heal me, and use what little I have to feed somebody else. Amen.

days.day: Saint Francis Xavier, Priest on Thursday of the 1st week of Advent
days.name: Saint Francis Xavier
days.week: Thursday of the 1st week of Advent

passages.label: GOSPEL
verses: Not every one that saith to me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven: but he that doth the will of my Father who is in heaven, he shall enter into the kingdom of heaven.
Every one therefore that heareth these my words, and doth them, shall be likened to a wise man that built his house upon a rock,
And the rain fell, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and they beat upon that house, and it fell not, for it was founded on a rock.
And every one that heareth these my words, and doth them not, shall be like a foolish man that built his house upon the sand,
And the rain fell, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and they beat upon that house, and it fell, and great was the fall thereof.

saint.name: Saint Francis Xavier
saint.about: A Spanish priest from Navarre who met Saint Ignatius of Loyola as a student in Paris and became one of the first Jesuits. He sailed to India and preached in Goa and across Asia, then brought the Gospel to Japan. He died on an island off the coast of China, still trying to get in. He's a patron of the missions.

key.label: GOSPEL
key.v: a wise man that built his house upon a rock, And the rain fell, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and they beat upon that house, and it fell not, for it was founded on a rock.

days.title: BUILT ON ROCK
days.t: Jesus says saying Lord, Lord isn't enough. The one who hears his words and does them is like a man who built his house on rock: the storm hits and it stands.
days.where: This is the end of the Sermon on the Mount, the long teaching Jesus gives on a hill in Galilee. He closes it with the story of two houses, one on rock and one on sand. The first reading from Isaiah sings about a strong city whose walls are God himself.
days.means: Storms come for everybody: breakups, bills, a death in the family. Both houses got hit. The only difference was what they stood on. Going to Mass and praying is the foundation. Living it out on a Tuesday is what keeps the house up.
days.today: Pick one thing Jesus asks that you already know you should do, and actually do it today.
days.say: Saint Francis Xavier, pray for us. Jesus, let me not just hear you but do what you say, so when the storm comes I'm still standing. Amen.
